subject: dads who coach little league
tagline: Netflix for dads who coach little league
one_liner: Prestige television for a season that ended 3–11.
brand_voice_notes: Speak like a film distributor acquiring a difficult but important body of work. Treat every volunteer coach as an auteur and every mundane baseball decision as a six-part documentary. Dry, specific, composed. Never explain the joke.

hero.h1: Your pitching change deserves a six-part series.
hero.sub: Tape turns little league footage into prestige television for the dads who coached it. AI adds the score, the slow zoom and the suggestion that it all meant something.

features.title: A director’s cut of the bunt.
features.blurb: Our AI finds the seven seconds you keep talking about and expands them into 48 minutes. Includes three angles of the same angle.

features.title: Every assistant gets an antagonist arc.
features.blurb: A second opinion on the batting order becomes a season-long rivalry. The algorithm has reviewed the handshake and found it cold.

features.title: Autoplay through the offseason.
features.blurb: The next episode begins before anyone can suggest watching something else. Your family’s remote privileges return in April.

demo_screen_concept: A film-subscription library for Coach Dennis: a large featured documentary called The Pitching Change, two other films called Rain Delay and The Bunt, genre filters, search, a My List view and add/remove controls. Play opens an accessible modal with four timed mock scenes, each a still with editorial narration, progress, pause/resume, next scene and a drama-level toggle that changes the captions. A second generated still shows a rain-soaked coach on the bench. No real video or external requests.

design_direction.style: Film-society editorial. Butter-yellow programme pages, burgundy serif titles, pale-blue rectangular controls and generous landscape film stills. A subscription cinema programme rather than a sports broadcast.
design_direction.archetype: Subscription streaming landing, adapted from the bundled Video-First Hero: centered typographic opening, full-width film still with a separate programme caption, three editorial feature passages, subscriber credits and a membership comparison.
design_direction.motion_vocab: 180ms colour and opacity responses to controls. User-triggered mock scene progression only; no ambient motion. Reduced motion disables CSS transitions.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Centered large serif headline in a shallow butter-yellow opening, then one wide landscape still. The photograph and its title sit in separate rows so all copy remains legible. A burgundy programme band frames the film. Lower copy is left aligned with generous gaps, testimonials form a credits strip, and pricing is a subscription ledger. Mobile stacks in reading order.
design_direction.design_review: Used the bundled Video-First Hero recommendation for the streaming product, adapted to a still rather than real video. Rejected the default black-and-red cinema palette and condensed sports type: yesterday used sports-broadcast black. Selected custom butter, burgundy and blue with the library Magazine Style pairing. No full tuple matches the latest seven. Frontend-design review replaced an initial cream-and-clay proposal with this distinct film-programme palette; no decorative numbered features or tracked uppercase labels.

images.rationale: Hero: one cinema still earns the programme’s full-width film frame and is reused for the featured demo film. Demo: one separate rain-delay still; The Bunt uses an HTML/SVG scorebook treatment. Testimonials: one corporate coach portrait anchors the subscriber credits; other subscribers use initials. Three of four available image slots used.

items.prompt: Editorial photograph on 35mm film, a single middle-aged little league dad coach in an unbranded burgundy windbreaker and plain cap standing alone on a dusty community baseball mound, holding a baseball, staring gravely toward the empty dugout. Landscape composition, coach on the right third, empty field on the left, no other people. Late afternoon pale butter-yellow light #F2E9BD, burgundy fabric #5A2035, pale blue sky #B7D1E5. Subtle film grain, authentic municipal field, restrained cinema-journal art direction, human proportions and natural hands. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens.
items.judge_verdict: Pass: correct coach subject, harmonious palette and mood, no visible text artifacts or anatomy defects.
